title: Incremental customer usage export: efficient S3 CSV partitioning + resilient webhook delivery/backpressure
creator: Maya Chen
description: Customers have requested scheduled and incremental usage exports with predictable S3 layouts (time/customer partitioning) and a webhook delivery option that tolerates receiver backpressure. Current export subsystem emits full daily CSVs and a best-effort webhook that frequently duplicates data and fails under slow consumers. This ticket scopes the backend changes for incremental delta exports, strong idempotency, S3 multipart uploads and partitioned object keys, webhook delivery with leaky-bucket backpressure handling and exponential-jitter retries, and improved audit/manifest records so customers can reconcile exports to billing dashboards.
background_and_rationale: We currently ship full exports for large customers which is costly and slow; customers on dedicated plans want smaller incremental deltas to minimize egress and processing. Several support incidents in Q4 2024 showed webhook receivers dropping events under load; we need server-side throttling and clear retry semantics. Additionally, storage and retrieval patterns for large orgs become inefficient without consistent S3 partitioning and object naming conventions. This work reduces per-customer egress, improves delivery reliability for push integrations, and unlocks scheduled near-real-time exports for analytics teams.
design_decisions_and_tradeoffs: Use a cursor-based incremental export model: store per-customer high-water mark in Postgres (single row) for correctness and auditability vs using Redis which risks volatile state.
Partition S3 by customer_id/YYYY/MM/DD and include manifest.json for each run to make downstream consumption deterministic; this increases small-file count but improves discoverability.

Implement at-least-once delivery semantics for webhooks with idempotency keys in payloads. Accept at-least-once for simplicity and ask customers to be idempotent; at-most-once would require stronger two-phase ack flow and complexity.
Webhook backpressure: implement in-flight window + leaky-bucket queue per-customer-endpoint to avoid global instability; will cap concurrent deliveries per destination.
Retries: exponential backoff with randomized jitter and a max TTL (48 hours) before switching to pull/export retry and notifying customer via console/alert.
Encrypt manifests and CSV objects via customer KMS when customer has Private deployment or KMS configured; default server-side SSE for hosted customers.
We will support CSV and newline-delimited JSON (NDJSON) outputs for customers needing structured ingestion; CSV remains default for analytics spreadsheets.
Strong schema versioning in manifest to allow future column additions without breaking consumers; collectors should read by column name, not position.
Avoid immediate global rollout: start with opt-in beta for top 20 customers, gather telemetry, then broad rollout.
We will reuse existing export-worker autoscaling primitives where possible to avoid introducing a second scaling system.
Tradeoff: per-customer state in Postgres increases operational load but simplifies guarantees and reconciliation. We'll monitor connection/row growth and shard if needed.
S3 multipart upload for exports larger than 100MB to improve upload reliability and reduce retry times.
We will record export-level telemetry (tokens, rows, bytes, latency, webhook status) into the metrics pipeline for Console dashboards and anomaly detection.
Retention/archival policy: expose per-customer retention (30/90/365 days) and implement lifecycle rules on export buckets; removal is a separate compliance flow.
Security review is required due to PII potential and cross-account S3 connections; KMS integration and least privilege IAM roles will be part of the implementation.

We will not implement real-time streaming for webhooks in this phase; the focus is on scheduled delta exports + reliable push delivery with bounded retries. Real-time streaming is tracked in a follow-up ticket.
Document compatibility guarantees clearly in Console to avoid downstream breakage for legacy consumers.
Expose API to programmatically request replays for missed intervals using the manifest/offset information.
We will implement Owner + Admin RBAC checks so only authorized users can create scheduled exports or configure webhook endpoints.
We will support per-export customer-visible audit logs (Console) and internal audit events (SIEM) for compliance teams.
Observability: include trace propagation for export orchestration, delivery adapter, and S3 uploads to help debug failed deliveries.
We will add cost accounting tags to objects to attribute S3 egress costs to customer billing in daily reports.
Webhook payload size limits will be enforced; for large exports the system prefers S3 pointers (signed URLs) delivered over webhook rather than payload in-line.
We will expose export health and next-run schedule in the Console and send admin-facing alerts on repeated failures.
Compatibility: CSV column set will be stable per schema version; new columns are appended, and manifest.schema contains column metadata and sample types.
We will store exports for a minimum of 7 days after run for immediate replays; longer retention flows require paid add-ons.
We will add optional customer-provided webhook HMAC secrets to validate requests at receiver side.
We will implement a graceful degradation policy: when a webhook destination is repeatedly unavailable, we switch to S3 pointer mode and notify the customer.
We will expose export run cost estimate in Console before starting long historical replays to avoid surprise bills.
We will include CSV gzipping to reduce bandwidth; manifest will indicate compression and encoding.
We will avoid per-record transactional guarantees across heterogeneous destinations; instead guarantee per-run manifest correctness and idempotency keys for dedup at consumer side.
implementation_plan: Week 1: Finalize design doc and schema in Confluence; engineering sign-off and security review kickoff.
Week 2: Add export cursor table + migration + basic incremental exporter that writes NDJSON to s3-staging bucket (PoC).
Week 3: Build Delivery Adapter interface (S3/CSV writer, Webhook sender) and integration tests; add idempotency key generation.
Week 4: Implement webhook leaky-bucket per-endpoint + retry scheduler with exponential jitter; add metrics and tracing hooks.
Week 5: Add multipart uploads, gzipping, and manifest.json generation; implement manifest schema versioning.
Week 6: End-to-end QA with top 3 customers in beta; load test webhook backpressure scenarios and S3 scale tests.
Week 7: Rollout opt-in beta in Console UI; monitoring dashboards, alerts, and support runbooks prepared.
Week 8: Gradual rollout to all customers, monitor cost and failure metrics, follow-up bugfix sprint.
Post-rollout: Add API endpoints for replay, export templates, and per-export RBAC controls in subsequent tickets.
acceptance_criteria: Export runs can be scheduled per-customer with retention and output format selection (CSV or NDJSON) via Console or API.
Incremental exports emit only delta records relative to last successful run per-customer (cursor stored in Postgres).
S3 object keys follow the agreed pattern: s3://<exports-bucket>/customer_id/YYYY/MM/DD/export-run-<run_id>.(csv|ndjson).gz and contain a manifest.json in the same prefix.
Manifest contains schema version, column metadata, row_count, bytes, compression, run_id, start_ts, end_ts, and cursor_high_water_mark.
Webhook delivery obeys per-endpoint concurrency limits; failed deliveries are retried with exponential jitter and observable retry metrics.
Webhook payloads include an idempotency_key per record and a run-level idempotency token for deduplication by receivers.
For endpoints that remain unreachable after TTL, system switches to S3 pointer delivery and emits an admin alert with root cause hint.
All export artifacts for KMS-enabled customers are encrypted with the customer KMS key; test vectors validate encryption and decryption.
End-to-end integration tests cover multipart uploads and resume after transient S3/network failures without data duplication beyond at-least-once semantics.
Performance: incremental run for a 10M-token customer produces export artifacts within the configured SLA (6 hours for historical replays, next-run delta under 15 minutes for scheduled runs).
Telemetry: metrics emitted to existing dashboards include runs.success, runs.failed, webhook.attempts, webhook.latency, s3.bytes_uploaded, s3.multipart_retries.
Console shows recent runs, last successful cursor, and provides a replay button that can trigger a re-run for a selected interval with a cost estimate.
Security: security review sign-off recorded and IAM roles scoped to least privilege for export workers and cross-account S3 access.
